questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following coordinate complexes is heteroleptic?
questions.solution:
A homoleptic complex has only one type of ligand attached to the central metal atom or ion.

A heteroleptic complex has more than one type of ligand attached to the central metal atom or ion.

Pentacarbonyliron(0) is $[Fe(CO)_5]$, which has only $CO$ ligands (homoleptic).

Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is $[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$, which has two different types of ligands, $NH_3$ and $NO_2^{-}$ (heteroleptic).

Tetraamminecopper(II) ion is $[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$, which has only $NH_3$ ligands (homoleptic).

Tetracyanonickelate(II) ion is $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$, which has only $CN^{-}$ ligands (homoleptic).

Thus, Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is the heteroleptic complex.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following complex is neutral?
questions.solution:
A neutral complex is a coordination compound that does not have an overall electrical charge and does not dissociate into ions in solution.

$\text{K}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]$ is an ionic complex that dissociates into $3\text{K}^+$ and $[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]^{3-}$ ions.

$[\text{Zn(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ is a cationic complex with a $+2$ charge.

$[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ is a cationic complex with a $+2$ charge.

$[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$ has no overall charge and no counter ions, making it a neutral complex.

Answer: $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the coordination number of central metal ion in $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$ complex ?
questions.solution:
The given complex is $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$.

The ligand 'en' stands for ethylenediamine, which is a bidentate ligand. This means each 'en' molecule coordinates to the central metal ion through two donor nitrogen atoms.

Since there are three 'en' ligands attached to the central cobalt ion, the total number of coordinate bonds formed is $3 \times 2 = 6$.

Therefore, the coordination number of the central metal ion is $6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the formula of Bis(ethylenediamine)dithiocyanatoplatinum(IV)ion from following.
questions.solution:
The central metal ion is Platinum in the $+4$ oxidation state, denoted as $\text{Pt}^{4+}$.

The ligands are:
Bis(ethylenediamine) → two ethylenediamine (en) molecules. Since 'en' is a neutral ligand, its charge contribution is $0$.
dithiocyanato → two thiocyanato ($\text{SCN}^{-}$) ions. Each $\text{SCN}^{-}$ has a charge of $-1$, so their total charge contribution is $-2$.

The net charge on the complex ion is calculated as:
Net charge = Charge of Pt + Charge of $2(\text{en})$ + Charge of $2(\text{SCN}^{-})$
Net charge = $+4 + 0 + 2(-1) = +2$

Writing the formula by placing the central metal atom followed by the ligands in alphabetical order inside the coordination sphere, we get:
$[\text{Pt(en)}_2(\text{SCN})_2]^{2+}$

Answer: $[\text{Pt(en)}_2(\text{SCN})_2]^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following complexes is an example of $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ type distereoisomers ?
questions.solution:
The general formula $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ represents an octahedral complex with one central metal atom $\text{M}$, four identical ligands $\text{A}$, and two different ligands $\text{B}$ and $\text{C}$.

Analyzing the given options:

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)(\text{H}_2\text{O})\,\text{Cl}_2]$ is of the type $\text{MA}_2\text{BC}$ (where $\text{A} = \text{Cl}$, $\text{B} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{C} = \text{H}_2\text{O}$).

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{ClBr}]^{2+}$ is of the type $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$, $\text{C} = \text{Br}$).

$\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\,\text{Cl}_2$ is of the type $\text{MA}_2\text{B}_2$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$).

$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is of the type $\text{MA}_4\text{B}_2$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$).

Thus, $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{ClBr}]^{2+}$ is the example of $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ type complex, which exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms), and these geometrical isomers are diastereoisomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following coordinate complexes contains neutral ligand ?
questions.solution:
Pentacarbonyliron (0) has the formula $[Fe(CO)_5]$. The ligand present is carbonyl (CO), which is a neutral molecule.

Hexacyanoferrate (II) ion has the formula $[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}$. The ligand is cyanide ($CN^-$), which is an anionic ligand.

Trioxalatocobaltate (III) ion has the formula $[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$. The ligand is oxalate ($C_2O_4^{2-}$), which is an anionic ligand.

Sodium hexanitrocobaltate (III) has the formula $Na_3[Co(NO_2)_6]$. The ligand is nitro ($NO_2^-$), which is an anionic ligand.

Therefore, only pentacarbonyliron (0) contains a neutral ligand.

Answer: Pentacarbonyliron (0)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of cobalt in $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ ?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of cobalt be $x$.

Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is a neutral ligand, so its charge is $0$.

The sum of the oxidation states of all atoms in the complex ion is equal to the net charge on the ion.

$x + 6(0) = +3$

$x = +3$

The oxidation state of cobalt in $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of hybridization is found in $[\text{Ni}(\text{Cl})_4]^{2-}$?
questions.solution:
The given complex is $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$.

Let the oxidation state of Ni be $x$.

$x + 4(-1) = -2 \Rightarrow x = +2$

The electronic configuration of neutral Ni is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of Ni$^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$.

Cl$^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so it does not cause the pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals of Ni$^{2+}$.

To accommodate the four electron pairs donated by the four Cl$^{-}$ ligands, the Ni$^{2+}$ ion undergoes hybridization using one $4s$ and three $4p$ empty orbitals.

Therefore, the hybridization involved is $sp^3$, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry.

Answer: $sp^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct increasing order of ligand field strength ?
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the ligands are arranged in the increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) or ligand field strength as follows:

$I^{-} \lt Br^{-} \lt SCN^{-} \lt Cl^{-} \lt S^{2-} \lt F^{-} \lt OH^{-} \lt C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^{-} \lt EDTA^{4-} \lt NH_3 \lt en \lt CN^{-} \lt CO$

From the given options, the correct increasing order of ligand field strength is:

$C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt EDTA \lt en$

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{EDTA} \lt \text{en}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is EAN for metal ion in $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ ?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of iron (Fe) is $26$.

Let the oxidation state of Fe in $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ be $x$.

$x + 6(-1) = -3$

$x = +3$

The formula for Effective Atomic Number (EAN) is:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{Oxidation state} + 2 \times (\text{Coordination number})$

$\text{EAN} = 26 - 3 + 2 \times 6$

$\text{EAN} = 23 + 12 = 35$

Answer: $35$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find EAN of Fe in $\text{Fe(CO)}_5$
questions.solution:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) is calculated using the formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{Oxidation State} + 2 \times \text{Coordination Number}$

For $\text{Fe(CO)}_5$:

Atomic number of Fe ($Z$) = $26$

Oxidation state of Fe = $0$ (since CO is a neutral ligand)

Coordination number = $5$

$\text{EAN} = 26 - 0 + 2 \times 5$

$\text{EAN} = 26 + 10 = 36$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a ligand with highest field strength among the following.
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the arrangement of ligands in the increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) values is:

$I^- \lt Br^- \lt SCN^- \lt Cl^- \lt S^{2-} \lt F^- \lt OH^- \lt C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^- \lt edta^{4-} \lt NH_3 \lt en \lt CN^- \lt CO$

From the given options, the order of field strength is $S^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^- \lt NH_3$.

Thus, $\text{NH}_3$ has the highest field strength.

Answer: $\text{NH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a ligand with lowest field strength among the following.
questions.solution:
The field strength of ligands is determined by the spectrochemical series, which arranges ligands in order of increasing field strength.

The spectrochemical series is given as:
$\text{I}^- \lt \text{Br}^- \lt \text{SCN}^- \lt \text{Cl}^- \lt \text{S}^{2-} \lt \text{F}^- \lt \text{OH}^- \lt \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{NCS}^- \lt \text{edta}^{4-} \lt \text{NH}_3 \lt \text{en} \lt \text{CN}^- \lt \text{CO}$

Comparing the given ligands based on the series, the order of field strength is:
$\text{Br}^- \lt \text{OH}^- \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{en}$

Therefore, $\text{Br}^-$ has the lowest field strength among the given options.

Answer: $\text{Br}^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the EAN of metal ion in $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ ?
questions.solution:
The effective atomic number (EAN) is calculated using the formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{O.S.} + 2 \times \text{C.N.}$

For the complex $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$:
Atomic number of copper ($Z$) = $29$
Oxidation state of copper ($\text{O.S.}$) = $+2$
Coordination number ($\text{C.N.}$) = $4$

Substituting the values:

$\text{EAN} = 29 - 2 + 2 \times 4$

$\text{EAN} = 27 + 8 = 35$

Answer: $35$

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{O.S.} + 2 \times \text{C.N.}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of ligands which are directly bonded to the metal is known as
questions.solution:
The number of ligand donor atoms to which the metal is directly bonded is defined as the co-ordination number of the metal in the complex.

For example, in the complex ion $[PtCl_6]^{2-}$, the co-ordination number of platinum is $6$ because it is directly bonded to six chloride ligands.

Answer: co-ordination number

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the ionization isomer of $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}(\text{NO}_2)]\,\text{Cl}$ from the following.
questions.solution:
Ionization isomerism occurs when a ligand inside the coordination sphere is exchanged with an anion outside the coordination sphere (counter ion), resulting in a complex that yields different ions in solution.

In the given complex $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}(\text{NO}_2)]\,\text{Cl}$, the counter ion is $\text{Cl}^-$ and the ligands are $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{Cl}^-$, and $\text{NO}_2^-$.

By exchanging the $\text{NO}_2^-$ ligand inside the coordination sphere with the $\text{Cl}^-$ counter ion outside, we get the ionization isomer $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}_2]\,(\text{NO}_2)$.

The original complex yields $\text{Cl}^-$ ions in aqueous solution, whereas its ionization isomer yields $\text{NO}_2^-$ ions.

Answer: $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}_2]\,(\text{NO}_2)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify oxidation state of cobalt ion in the complex, $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ .
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of cobalt be $x$.

The given coordination compound dissociates into a complex cation $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]^{2+}$ and a sulfate anion $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$.

The overall charge on the complex cation is $+2$.

Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is a neutral ligand with an oxidation state of $0$, and bromide ($\text{Br}^-$) has an oxidation state of $-1$.

Summing the oxidation states of the central metal atom and the ligands:

$x + 5(0) + (-1) = +2$

$x - 1 = +2$

$x = +3$

The oxidation state of cobalt in the complex is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the number of unpaired electrons present and geometry respectively of $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ complex.
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of Co in $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is $+3$.

The electronic configuration of Co is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of Co$^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.

Since $\text{NH}_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for Co$^{3+}$, pairing of electrons takes place in the $3d$ subshell.

All $6$ electrons pair up in the inner $d$-orbitals, leaving two $3d$ orbitals empty.

The number of unpaired electrons is $0$.

The complex undergoes $d^2sp^3$ hybridization, resulting in an octahedral geometry.

Answer: 0, octahedral

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ligands splits d orbitals to maximum level?
questions.solution:
The splitting of d orbitals depends on the strength of the ligand, which is given by the spectrochemical series.

The order of ligand strength for the given options is $\text{Cl}^- \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{NH}_3 \lt \text{CN}^-$.

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is the strongest field ligand among the given options, it causes the maximum crystal field splitting of the d orbitals.

Answer: $\text{CN}^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the complex having the highest number of unpaired electrons from following.
questions.solution: In $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, Co is in $+3$ oxidation state with $3d^6$ configuration. Since NH_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for Co$^{3+}$, pairing of electrons takes place resulting in $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ configuration. Number of unpaired electrons $= 0$. \\  \\ In $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, Co is in $+3$ oxidation state with $3d^6$ configuration. F$^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs. The configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$. Number of unpaired electrons $= 4$. \\  \\ In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in $+2$ oxidation state with $3d^8$ configuration. Cl$^-$ is a weak field ligand, forming a tetrahedral complex with $e^4 t_2^4$ configuration. Number of unpaired electrons $= 2$. \\  \\ In $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in $+2$ oxidation state with $3d^8$ configuration. CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, forming a square planar complex where all electrons are paired. Number of unpaired electrons $= 0$. \\  \\ Thus, $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ has the highest number of unpaired electrons. \\  \\ Answer: $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the coordination complex, Potassium hexacyanoferrate(II), the central atom/ion acts as,
questions.solution:
The coordination complex is Potassium hexacyanoferrate(II), which is $K_4[Fe(CN)_6]$.

The central metal ion is $Fe^{2+}$ and the ligands are $CN^{-}$ ions.

In the formation of a coordination complex, the central metal ion accepts electron pairs from the ligands to form coordinate covalent bonds.

According to the Lewis acid-base theory, an electron pair acceptor is a Lewis acid.

Therefore, the central atom/ion acts as a Lewis acid.

Answer: Lewis acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The sum of coordination number and oxidation number of M in $[\text{M(en)}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4]\text{Cl}$ is
questions.solution:
In the given complex $[\text{M(en)}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4]\text{Cl}$, the ligands present inside the coordination sphere are ethylenediamine (en) and oxalate ($\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$).

Both ethylenediamine and oxalate are bidentate ligands.
Coordination number of M = $2 \times 2$ (from en) + $1 \times 2$ (from oxalate) = $4 + 2 = 6$.

To find the oxidation number of M, let its oxidation state be $x$.
The charge on ethylenediamine is $0$, the charge on oxalate is $-2$, and the charge on the chloride ion outside the coordination sphere is $-1$.
Equating the sum of oxidation states to the overall charge of the neutral compound:
$x + 2(0) + 1(-2) + 1(-1) = 0$
$x - 3 = 0$
$x = +3$

The oxidation number of M is $3$.

Sum of coordination number and oxidation number = $6 + 3 = 9$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ ?
options: It is $sp^3 d^2$ hybridised and tetrahedral.
It is $d^2 sp^3$ hybridised and octahedral.
It is $dsp^2$ hybridised and square planar
It is $sp^3 d^2$ hybridised and octahedral.
questions.solution:
The given complex is $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$.

Let the oxidation state of Mn be $x$.

$x + 6(-1) = -3 \Rightarrow x = +3$

The electronic configuration of Mn is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$.

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals against Hund's rule. The four electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, leaving two $e_g$ orbitals empty.

These two empty $3d$ orbitals, along with one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals, undergo $d^2sp^3$ hybridization.

The geometry corresponding to $d^2sp^3$ hybridization is octahedral.

Answer: It is $d^2 sp^3$ hybridised and octahedral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following comparisons is correct for $\Delta_0$ of the following complexes?
I- $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$
II- $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$
III- $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$
IV- $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3+}$
questions.solution:
The crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_0$) depends on several factors, including the oxidation state of the central metal ion and the nature of the ligands.

1. Oxidation state of the metal ion: For the same metal and ligand, $\Delta_0$ increases with an increase in the oxidation state of the central metal ion. This is because a higher charge on the metal ion draws the ligands closer, leading to greater repulsion and a larger splitting of the d-orbitals.
In complex I, Co is in the $+2$ oxidation state: $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$.
In complex II, Co is in the $+3$ oxidation state: $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$.
Therefore, $\Delta_0$ of II > I, which means $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$ is a correct comparison.

2. Nature of the ligand: Strong field ligands cause a larger splitting than weak field ligands. $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, whereas $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand.
Thus, $\Delta_0$ of $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3+}$ (IV) is significantly greater than that of $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ (II) and $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ (III). The comparison $\text{IV} \lt \text{II}$ is incorrect.

3. The comparison $\text{II} \lt \text{I}$ is incorrect based on the oxidation state rule.

Thus, the most appropriate and direct standard comparison is $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$.

Answer: $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of color is observed when a compound absorbs red coloured light?
questions.solution:
When a compound absorbs a specific color of light from the visible spectrum, the color it exhibits (observed color) is the complementary color of the absorbed light.

According to the complementary color wheel, the complementary color of red is blue-green (or cyan). For example, hydrated copper(II) complexes absorb red light and appear blue.

Since blue-green is not explicitly given in the options, blue is the most appropriate and closest choice.

Answer: Blue

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following sets of ligands does NOT contain ambident ligand in it?
questions.solution:
An ambidentate ligand is a ligand that has more than one type of donor atom and can bind to the central metal ion through any of these different donor atoms.

Examples of ambidentate ligands include $\text{NO}_2^-$ (which can bind through N or O) and $\text{NCS}^-$ (which can bind through N or S).

Checking the given options:
Option 1 contains $\text{NO}_2^-$ and $\text{NCS}^-$, both of which are ambidentate ligands.
Option 2 contains $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ (binds only through O), ethylene diamine (binds only through N), and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (binds only through O). None of these are ambidentate ligands.
Option 3 contains $\text{NO}_2^-$, which is an ambidentate ligand.
Option 4 contains $\text{NCS}^-$, which is an ambidentate ligand.

Therefore, the set containing $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$, ethylene diamine, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ does not contain any ambidentate ligand.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an ambident ligand ?
questions.solution:
An ambident ligand is a monodentate ligand that contains more than one coordinating atom and can bind to the central metal ion through different atoms.

Ethylene diamine is a bidentate ligand coordinating through two nitrogen atoms.

$\text{Cl}^-$ is a monodentate ligand coordinating only through the chlorine atom.

EDTA is a hexadentate ligand coordinating through two nitrogen and four oxygen atoms.

$\text{SCN}^-$ (thiocyanate ion) can coordinate to the central metal ion either through the sulfur atom (thiocyanato) or through the nitrogen atom (isothiocyanato). Therefore, it is an ambident ligand.

Answer: SCN

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a complex compound, central metal ion is
questions.solution:
In a complex compound, the central metal ion accepts one or more electron pairs from the surrounding ligands to form coordinate covalent bonds.

According to the Lewis theory of acids and bases, an electron pair acceptor is defined as a Lewis acid, while an electron pair donor is defined as a Lewis base.

Therefore, the central metal ion acts as a Lewis acid.

Answer: Lewis acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the hybridization in central metal of $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$ complex.
questions.solution:
In $[Fe(CO)_5]$, the central metal atom is $Fe$ and its oxidation state is $0$.

The ground state electronic configuration of $Fe$ is $[Ar] 3d^6 4s^2$.

$CO$ is a strong field ligand, which causes the pairing of electrons.

The two $4s$ electrons shift to the $3d$ subshell and pair up, resulting in a $3d^8$ configuration. Four $3d$ orbitals are completely filled and one $3d$ orbital is left empty.

To accommodate the five electron pairs from the five $CO$ ligands, one $3d$, one $4s$, and three $4p$ orbitals hybridize.

Therefore, the hybridization is $dsp^3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following complexes contains anionic ligand?
questions.solution:
To identify the complex containing an anionic ligand, examine the charge characteristics of each ligand in the coordination sphere.
In the tetraamminecopper(II) ion $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}_3)4]^{2+}$, the ammine ligand $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is neutral.
The pentaammineaquacobalt(III) iodide complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)5(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})]^{3+}$ contains neutral ammine and aqua ligands $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.
In tetracyanonickelate(II) ion $[\mathrm{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$, the cyano ligand $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ carries a $-1$ charge, confirming its anionic character.
Pentacarbonyliron(0) $[\mathrm{Fe(CO)}_{5}]$ features the neutral carbonyl ligand $\mathrm{CO}$.
The tetracyanonickelate(II) ion is the only complex with an anionic ligand.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following complexes does NOT obey EAN rule?
questions.solution:
Effective Atomic Number analysis determines which complex violates the noble gas electron count rule.

The EAN equals the sum of metal valence electrons and ligand-donated electrons, aiming for Kr (36), Xe (54), or Rn (86). For monodentate ligands: $\text{EAN} = Z_{\text{metal}} - \text{oxidation state} + 2 \times \text{number of ligands}$.

For $\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6^{3+}$: Co atomic number 27, oxidation state +3 gives 24 valence electrons; 6 $\mathrm{NH}_3$ donate 12 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 24 + 12 = 36$, satisfying the rule.

For $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CO})_6$: Cr atomic number 24, oxidation state 0 gives 24 valence electrons; 6 CO donate 12 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 24 + 12 = 36$, satisfying the rule.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

Combining larger size and absence of CFSE, $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$ forms the least stable complex.

questions.q: Find the total number of moles of donor atoms present in one mole trioxalatocobaltate(III) ion.
questions.solution:
In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3\right]^{3-}$, three oxalate ligands are attached to the cobalt ion. Since oxalate is a bidentate ligand, each $\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)^{2-}$ has two donor oxygen atoms.
1 mole of $\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)^{2-} \equiv 2$ moles of donor atoms.
$\therefore 1$ mole of $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3\right]^{3-} \equiv 3 \times 2=6$ moles of donor atoms.

Effective atomic number $=\mathrm{Z}-\mathrm{O} . \mathrm{N}+2 \mathrm{C} . \mathrm{N}\mathrm{Z}=$ Atomic number

C. $\mathrm{N}=$ Coordination number

& \mathrm{EAN}=27-3+2 \times 6=36
\end{aligned}

questions.solution:
Identifying a neutral complex requires calculating the total charge of each coordination entity. The overall charge is the sum of the central metal's oxidation state and the charges from all ligands.

For tetracyanonickelate(II) ion, the nickel center is Ni2+ and four CN– ligands contribute –4, yielding a –2 charge: $+2 + 4 \times (-1) = -2$, an anion.

Sodium hexafluoroaluminate(III) contains the complex ion [AlF6]3–, as aluminum is +3 and six F– ligands contribute –6: $+3 + 6 \times (-1) = -3$, an anion.

Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) has cobalt at +3, three neutral NH3 ligands, and three NO2– ligands contributing –3: $+3 + 3 \times 0 + 3 \times (-1) = 0$, a neutral complex.

Tetraamminecopper(II) ion features Cu2+ and four neutral NH3 ligands: $+2 + 4 \times 0 = +2$, a cation.

$\boxed{C}$ is the neutral complex.
